title: Walk through a visit in the Visit Wizard

claims.claim: Open the visit, work through the Visit Wizard's 17 sections, and finish with Sign & Lock.

checks.note: 17 sections only if there is no Step 2b

claims.finding: The wizard has 18 sections: Steps 1-17 plus Step 2b, Clinical History Review, between Steps 2 and 3 (VisitWizardV4.tsx:17115). The page itself sends allergies to section 2B.
claims.proposed_text: Open the visit, work through the Visit Wizard's sections (Steps 1–17, plus Step 2b, Clinical History Review), and finish with Sign & Lock.

claims.claim: To stop a visit you already started and do not intend to finish, cancel or delete the appointment — see Stop or cancel a visit you started.

checks.pattern: Cannot delete — this appointment has a visit note attached.
checks.note: deleting would be open to a started visit only if the server did not refuse it

claims.finding: A started visit cannot be deleted. update-appointment refuses delete when the appointment has a visit_data_v2 row ("Cannot delete — this appointment has a visit note attached. Cancel or Archive instead", update-appointment/index.ts:498-513), and the Appointment Management card disables Delete once a note is attached (AppointmentManagementCard.tsx:878). A draft is removed with Cancel visit or Archive.
claims.proposed_text: To stop a visit you already started and do not intend to finish, cancel the appointment or archive its draft — see Stop or cancel a visit you started. An appointment can be deleted only while no visit note is attached.

proposed_checks.pattern: Cannot delete — this appointment has a visit note attached.

claims.claim: Before you start — Have a way into the visit: Fleet Calendar — open the scheduled appointment.
Patient Management (My Clinical Day) — open the scheduled visit.
All Patients → Appointment Management — select the visit date, then click Open Visit.

checks.note: on-screen label is 'Open visit' (lower-case v)

claims.claim: Wound Cockpit — use Pick a visit or start a new one in the upper-right corner.

checks.pattern: Pick a visit or start a new one…

claims.claim: Turn on location services on your device. GPS access is required for geofence verification on in-person visits.

checks.note: GPS/geofence would be live only if the timer UI were not switched off

claims.finding: The visit timer and its GPS geofence are switched off: the timer UI is wrapped in `{false && ...}` (VisitWizardV4.tsx, "Timer Component — UI HIDDEN 2026-05-28"), so location is not needed to document a visit.
claims.proposed_text: Location services are not needed to document a visit. The visit timer and its GPS geofence are switched off in the Visit Wizard.

claims.claim: For a follow-up visit, review the wound's last visit first. Open the Wound Cockpit, select the wound case, click Details, and review the overview of the most recent visit.
Each section has a Mark as Complete button.

checks.note: 17 shared buttons + the Wound Assessment's own button would cover all 18 sections

claims.finding: 15 sections use the shared Mark as Complete button and Wound Assessment has its own (VisitWizardV4.tsx:17924). Step 1 Consent & Attestation and Step 16 LCD Audit & Review have none: Step 1 turns complete when a consent is on file (wizardRequiredFields.ts:236-239) and Step 16 when every other section is complete (VisitWizardV4.tsx:6280-6310).
claims.proposed_text: Most sections end with a Mark as Complete button. Step 1 (Consent & Attestation) and Step 16 (LCD Audit & Review) have none; they turn complete on their own.

claims.claim: In the section navigator, completed sections are green with a checkmark; sections that still need documentation or review are red.

checks.note: sections flagged for review would have to be red, not yellow

claims.finding: Completed sections are green with a checkmark. Sections flagged for review are yellow ("For Review" in the list, yellow in the progress bar); a red "Needs Attention" only appears for a validation error; untouched sections are grey "Pending" in the list and light red only in the top progress bar (VisitWizardV4.tsx:11107-11257, 16830-16840).
claims.proposed_text: Completed sections turn green with a checkmark. In the progress bar at the top, sections not yet complete show red and sections flagged for review show yellow.

claims.claim: From the Fleet Calendar: Tap the appointment tile. A popover shows the patient's name, appointment type, date, and time.

checks.note: the tile would open a popover

claims.finding: Tapping a tile opens the Appointment Details window (a modal dialog titled "Appointment Details", AppointmentDetailsModal.tsx:702, rendered from FleetCalendarCanvas.tsx), not a popover. Its footer button reads Start Visit, Continue Visit or Resume Visit by appointment status (appointmentActionVerb.ts).
claims.proposed_text: Tap the appointment tile. The Appointment Details window opens with the patient's name, appointment type, date, and time.

claims.claim: Click Start Visit at the bottom of the popover. The Visit Wizard opens for that patient and appointment.

checks.note: the tile would open a popover

claims.finding: Tapping a tile opens the Appointment Details window (a modal dialog titled "Appointment Details", AppointmentDetailsModal.tsx:702, rendered from FleetCalendarCanvas.tsx), not a popover. Its footer button reads Start Visit, Continue Visit or Resume Visit by appointment status (appointmentActionVerb.ts).
claims.proposed_text: Click Start Visit at the bottom of the window (it reads Continue Visit or Resume Visit when a note is already in progress). The Visit Wizard opens for that patient and appointment.

claims.claim: From the Wound Cockpit: Open the patient's Wound Cockpit. In the upper-right corner, open the dropdown Pick a visit or start a new one. Select the scheduled visit, or choose to start a new one. Click Open. The Visit Wizard opens, ready to begin or resume documentation.

checks.pattern: Pick a visit or start a new one…
"+ Start visit — pick a calendar slot…"

claims.claim: Pull Migration Data carries forward information documented at the patient's previous Medipyxis visits, so you don't re-enter it.

checks.note: the most recent visit would be offered only if the pre-filled visit were not excluded

claims.finding: The wizard already pre-fills a returning patient's visit from the most recent visit; Pull Migration Data lists only the earlier visits that pre-fill did not load ("Find prior visits for this patient that weren't auto-loaded.", PullMigrationDataButton.tsx:39; exclusion at VisitWizardV4.tsx:1814-1820). Pulling a visit copies only patient context, comorbidities and Braden score, functional status and patient education (projectVisit, wizardPrefillCascade.ts:1004-1040), even though the list summarises every section that holds data.
claims.proposed_text: The wizard pre-fills a returning patient's visit from their most recent visit automatically. Pull Migration Data finds the patient's other, earlier visits; pulling one copies its patient context, comorbidities, functional status, and patient education into this visit.

checks.note: a control labelled Pull Migration Data

claims.proposed_text: In the Pull Migration Data panel at the top of the wizard, click Find Prior Visits.

claims.claim: A window lists the patient's previous visits by date, with a summary of the sections that contain data.
Pick the most recent or most relevant visit and click Pull this visit.

checks.note: the most recent visit would be offered only if the pre-filled visit were not excluded

claims.finding: The most recent visit is never in the list: the visit the wizard already pre-filled from is excluded (VisitWizardV4.tsx:1814-1820).
claims.proposed_text: Pick the visit you need and click Pull this visit.

claims.claim: Pull Migration Data only uses visits documented in Medipyxis. It does not import records from another EHR.

checks.pattern: Some patients in the ND DrChrono migration have historical visits attached to a different patient record.
checks.note: the list would hold only visits documented in Medipyxis if it did not serve migrated EHR visits

claims.proposed_text: Pull Migration Data reads only visit records already stored in Medipyxis, including visits migrated from a previous EHR. It does not connect to another EHR.

claims.claim: Pulled data is a starting point, not a re-assessment. Review every pulled value against the patient in front of you before you sign.
Section 1 — Consent & Attestation: Use this section to obtain, record, or review the patient's consent for wound care services.

The consent form covers: General consent for treatment — wound care evaluation, treatment, and procedures. HIPAA notice of privacy practices. Wound photography and imaging consent. Insurance assignment of benefits. Financial responsibility.

checks.pattern: heading: "Photographs and Imaging of My Wounds",
heading: "Insurance, Assignment of Benefits, and Financial Responsibility",

claims.claim: The consent form covers: Telehealth consent, when the visit is virtual.

checks.note: a visit-type condition would have to be coded where the form is chosen or rendered

claims.finding: Telehealth is a fixed section of every consent edition (v1.en.ts:100-106); nothing in the capture dialog or the setting routing adds or removes it by visit type.
claims.proposed_text: Telehealth — how telehealth consultations work and their risks (part of every consent form).

claims.claim: Give the patient time to read the consent before they sign or authorize it.
Consent can also be captured before the visit, from the patient's chart — see Capture consent from the patient chart below.

Capture consent in the Visit Wizard: Review the patient's existing consent, if there is one, and decide whether a new consent is needed for this encounter. Choose how to capture it: Electronic signature — open the consent form, hand the patient your device to review it, and have them sign on screen. Confirm and save. Signed paper consent — record the paper consent, upload the signed document, and save. Verbal consent — complete the documentation steps and save.
Open the signed document, when there is one, to check it was recorded correctly.
Section 1: Click Mark as Complete.

checks.note: a Mark as Complete button in Section 1

claims.finding: Section 1 has no Mark as Complete button; it renders only the consent panel (VisitWizardV4.tsx:17011-17020). It turns complete on its own when a consent is on file (wizardRequiredFields.ts:236-239).
claims.proposed_text: Section 1 has no Mark as Complete button. It turns complete once a consent is on file.

claims.claim: Capture consent from the patient chart: You can collect consent before the visit without opening the Visit Wizard. Click All Patients in the left menu, find the patient, and click View on their card.
On the Clinical Overview tab, find the Consent section. It shows the current consent and its date.

Choose a method: Re-sign — the patient reviews and signs electronically on your device. Record a paper consent — document and upload a consent the patient already signed on paper. Send Consent SMS — confirm the patient's mobile number and send a link they open on their phone to review and sign. Check the Consent section afterwards to confirm it was received. Verbal by phone — record consent given over the phone.
Click Open signed document to view the recorded consent.

Record verbal consent only where your organization's policies and the law allow it for that treatment. General wound care consent does not replace separate informed consent that some advanced or invasive procedures require.
Section 2 — Patient Context / Demographics: Select the Visit Type: Initial, Follow-up, Post-op, or Re-eval.
claims.finding: Section 2 has no visit-type picker; the visit type comes from the appointment and is passed to the wizard as visitTypeKey (openVisitWizard.ts; PatientDemographicsVisit.tsx:61-64).
claims.proposed_text: The visit type comes from the appointment; Section 2 does not ask for it.

claims.claim: Enter the Chief Complaint — a brief summary of the reason for the visit.
Review insurance. Coverage is shown for reference and the secondary payer is read-only.

checks.pattern: title="Secondary payer is shown from the patient chart.

claims.claim: Make insurance changes on the patient's Insurance tab, not in the wizard.
claims.finding: The wizard sends insurance changes to the patient's Billing & Auth page ("To change insurance, use the patient's Billing & Auth page.", PatientDemographicsVisit.tsx:1598).
claims.proposed_text: Make insurance changes on the patient's Billing & Auth page, not in the wizard.

proposed_checks.pattern: To change insurance, use the patient's Billing & Auth page.

claims.claim: Section 2: Click Mark as Complete.
Allergies are reviewed in the next section, 2B — Clinical History Review, together with the patient's medical history.
Sections 3–6 — Clinical baseline: 3. Review of Systems — the body-system review with relevant symptoms and findings. Update anything carried forward from earlier visits.
4. Objective Assessment — Vital signs, vascular and perfusion exam, edema, ankle and calf circumference, ABI/TBI, vascular ultrasound results, HbA1c when applicable, and the vascular follow-up plan.
5. Functional Status & ADLs — Mobility, ambulation, independence with daily activities, fall risk, and limitations that affect wound care.

checks.note: a fall-risk field

claims.finding: Section 5 records mobility level, ambulation, ADL independence and mobility limitations (WoundCaseFunctionalStatusVisit.tsx:28-57, 352) but has no fall-risk field.
claims.proposed_text: 5. Functional Status & ADLs — Mobility, ambulation, independence with daily activities, and limitations that affect wound care.

claims.claim: 6. Comorbidities & Risk Factors — Conditions that contribute to the wound or slow healing — for example diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, chronic venous insufficiency, heart failure, lymphedema, nutritional deficiencies, and smoking status.

checks.note: lymphedema offered on the step

claims.finding: Diabetes, PAD, CVI, congestive heart failure, malnutrition and smoking are on the step (WoundCaseRiskFactorsVisit.tsx:455-493, 1446), but lymphedema is not offered anywhere in Section 6.
claims.proposed_text: 6. Comorbidities & Risk Factors — Conditions that contribute to the wound or slow healing — for example diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, chronic venous insufficiency, heart failure, malnutrition, and smoking status.

claims.claim: These sections ... support the treatment plan and the medical necessity documentation that Medicare LCDs ask for.
What Section 4 covers: Vital signs — blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, height, weight, and BMI.
Vascular and perfusion exam — peripheral pulses, perfusion, and signs of arterial or venous insufficiency.

Edema — the affected limb and location, severity, and pitting or non-pitting. Measure ankle and calf circumference for a baseline and repeat it at follow-ups to track the response to treatment such as compression.
ABI / TBI — enter results from earlier vascular studies or from measurements taken at the visit. Use them to decide whether compression is appropriate.
Vascular ultrasound and duplex results — venous or arterial duplex findings, reflux, obstruction, or peripheral arterial disease.

checks.note: an arterial duplex entry

claims.finding: Section 4 has venous duplex only: "Venous duplex ultrasound and CEAP", for venous and mixed arterial-venous ulcers, per leg — performed/reviewed, study date, findings and CEAP clinical class (VenousDuplexFields.tsx:60-160). There is no arterial duplex entry.
claims.proposed_text: Venous duplex ultrasound and CEAP — for venous and mixed arterial-venous ulcers, per leg: whether a duplex was done or reviewed, the study date, the findings, and the CEAP clinical class.

proposed_checks.pattern: For venous and mixed arterial-venous ulcers. Recorded separately for

claims.claim: Vascular management and follow-up plan — choose all that apply and add details: Referral ordered; Already under vascular care; Further assessment planned; Intervention completed; Referral or intervention deferred (clinical judgement); Patient declined, or an access barrier.

checks.pattern: label: "Patient declined, or an access barrier",

claims.claim: HbA1c — for patients with diabetes, the most recent result, as part of assessing glycemic control.
ABI/TBI results belong in Section 4 — Objective Assessment, not in Section 8 — Previous Treatments.
Completing these fields supports LCD documentation but does not by itself meet every LCD requirement; check the criteria for the wound type, treatment, and your Medicare Administrative Contractor.
Mark each section complete once it is documented.
Section 7 — Wound Assessment: Confirm wound etiology and staging. Stage drives the ICD-10 selection downstream.

checks.pattern: // Stage-aware ICD-10 resolver for the billing wizard.

claims.claim: Set the wound's Treating / Monitoring status. A wound marked Monitoring carries a yellow pill and relaxes some required fields for that visit; flip it back to Treating at any time.
Measure today. Enter Length (cm), Width (cm), and Depth (cm).
Photo upload is required if your facility policy mandates it.
claims.finding: There is no facility photo policy. Photo Capture is a recommended field for every non-monitoring wound (wizardRequiredFields.ts:348-353) and enforcement is off (WIZARD_VALIDATION_DISABLED = true, wizardRequiredFields.ts:856), so a missing photo never blocks.
claims.proposed_text: Take or upload a wound photo. It is recommended for every wound you are treating (optional for Monitoring wounds) and does not block you from finishing.

proposed_checks.pattern: { path: "wounds", label: "Photo Capture", perWound: true, woundPath: "capturedPhotos", check: "custom",

claims.claim: Set tissue percentages by wound. Granulation / Slough / Necrotic / Epithelial / Eschar must sum to 100%.

checks.note: 'must' holds only if validation is enforced

claims.finding: The 100% rule exists (wizardRequiredFields.ts:790-806) but enforcement is off (WIZARD_VALIDATION_DISABLED = true, wizardRequiredFields.ts:856): a different total is flagged as advisory and does not stop you.
claims.proposed_text: Set tissue percentages by wound (Granulation, Slough, Necrotic, Epithelial, Eschar). They should total 100%; the wizard flags a different total but does not block you.

claims.claim: Confirm the precise anatomical location. The location field is editable — pick from the dropdown or type the specific area (for example, Right lateral malleolus).
claims.finding: Specific Area is locked read-only in Section 7; it changes only through the anatomical site picker opened by Change, which enforces an allow-list (CompactWoundCaseSetupVisit.tsx:4861, 4932-4950).
claims.proposed_text: Confirm the anatomical location. Specific Area is read-only here; click Change to pick a different site from the anatomical site picker.

claims.claim: Document exudate, pain, and infection signs.
Section 7: Click Mark as Complete.
Section 8 — Previous Treatments: This section records the wound care the patient has already had. It is the history that supports medical necessity for advanced wound therapies.

checks.pattern: Document medical necessity for advanced therapy and optionally record

claims.claim: Add previous treatments. Click Add previous treatments and record offloading, compression, debridement, earlier skin substitute applications, and other conservative care — including treatment from outside providers.

checks.pattern: Optional: Document prior care from outside providers

claims.claim: Document chronicity. Record how long the wound has been present (for example, at least four weeks) and the standard-of-care treatments already tried.

checks.note: a field in Section 8 for how long the wound has been present

claims.finding: Section 8 has no field for how long the wound has been present. The wound's age is computed from the Onset Date entered in Section 7 (PreviousTreatmentsVisit.tsx:519-528; CompactWoundCaseSetupVisit.tsx:5265-5268); Section 8 records each prior treatment with its own Duration (weeks).
claims.proposed_text: Document chronicity. Check the wound's Onset Date in Section 7 — the wizard works out how long the wound has been present from it. For each previous treatment, record how long it was tried (Duration (weeks)).

claims.claim: Write the medical necessity statement. Click Summarize prior treatments for a starting draft, or type it in the Medical Necessity Note field. Explain why advanced treatment is indicated, including how the patient responded to earlier treatment.
Attach supporting documents, such as earlier medical records or referral letters, when you have them.

checks.pattern: Upload medical records, referral letters, or treatment history

claims.claim: Section 8: Click Mark as Complete.
Section 9 — Interventions & Treatments: Document every wound-specific intervention performed at this visit. What you enter here builds the procedure note and feeds billing.

Select the wound. In Wound-Specific Documentation, use the wound dropdown if the patient has more than one active wound. Document each wound separately, and finish one wound before switching to the next.
Add an intervention. Under Conservative Treatments Performed Today, click Add Your First Intervention (or Add Intervention) and choose what you did.

The list covers debridement (sharp, enzymatic, mechanical, autolytic, chemical), negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT), topical antimicrobials, wound irrigation, advanced dressings, offloading and pressure relief, compression therapy, infection management, nutritional support and other adjuncts, patient and caregiver education, graft and skin substitute application, molecular therapy, and ultrasonic therapy (for example MIST or Arobella).

checks.note: a molecular therapy intervention

claims.finding: Every listed type exists except "molecular therapy": the closest entry is MolecuLight, a fluorescence imaging check (Detection Result, Fluorescence Type), not a therapy (ConservativeCareInterventionVisit.tsx:2219-2235). The list also has Pain Management and PRP Application, which the page omits.
claims.proposed_text: The list covers debridement (sharp, enzymatic, mechanical, autolytic, chemical), negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT), topical antimicrobials, wound irrigation, advanced dressings, offloading and pressure relief, compression therapy, infection management, pain management, nutritional support and other adjuncts, patient and caregiver education, graft and skin substitute application, PRP application, MolecuLight fluorescence imaging, and ultrasonic therapy (for example MIST or Arobella).

claims.claim: Complete the intervention's fields. Each intervention has its own required fields. They flow into the procedure note, and billable procedures are linked to their CPT code for review in Billing & Documentation. Click Done to save.
Repeat for each intervention on the same wound.
Generate the procedure note: In Interventions Performed Today, click Generate Procedure Note.
Review the narrative for accuracy against the care you actually provided.
To use your own wording instead, enter it in the intervention's Notes field and check Use My Exact Procedure Note. Your note is kept exactly as written and is not regenerated.

checks.note: the control as the page names it

claims.finding: The checkbox is "Use my exact procedure note (skip AI/template regeneration)" and sits under the generated Procedure Note text box for the wound, not on an intervention's Notes field (ConservativeCareInterventionVisit.tsx:3813-3848). Its text is printed verbatim in the note.
claims.proposed_text: To use your own wording instead, edit the generated Procedure Note and check Use my exact procedure note. Your text is printed in the note exactly as written and is not regenerated.

proposed_checks.pattern: Use my exact procedure note (skip AI/template regeneration).
When checked, this text is rendered verbatim in Section 20 of the note.

claims.claim: Address contributing factors: In Contributing Factors, set a status for each factor — Nutrition, Infection, Glucose control, Perfusion, and Other underlying conditions: Addressed (optionally note what you did); Pending / Follow-Up Required (the planned follow-up); Not Applicable (a brief reason).

{ status: 'addressed', label: 'Addressed', detailNeeded: false, detailPrompt: 'Actions taken (optional)' },

checks.note: on-screen wording: 'Pending – Follow-up Required'

checks.pattern: { status: 'not_applicable', label: 'Not applicable', detailNeeded: true, detailPrompt: 'Brief reason' },

claims.claim: Section 9: Click Mark as Complete when every intervention and contributing factor is documented.
Selecting a procedure does not mean it meets every billing requirement. You remain responsible for reviewing all procedure documentation before you sign.
Section 10 — Care Planning: Each active wound needs its own care plan. Select the wound in Wound-Specific Care Planning. Finish one wound's plan before moving to the next.

checks.note: the selector as the page names it

claims.finding: The wound selector is labelled "Select Wound for Care Planning:" under the "Care Plan Updates" heading (marked Wound-specific) (VisitWizardCarePlanningSection.tsx:1184-1217). Nothing is labelled Wound-Specific Care Planning.
claims.proposed_text: Each active wound needs its own care plan. Choose the wound in Select Wound for Care Planning (under Care Plan Updates). Finish one wound's plan before moving to the next.

claims.claim: Set the Follow-Up Interval (for example, weekly). The Next Visit Date fills in automatically — check it matches the schedule you intend.

checks.note: on-screen: 'Follow-up Interval'

claims.claim: Write the Treatment Plan Narrative. ... You can: Dictate — click the microphone in the upper-right corner of the field. Generate Draft — create a draft from the visit's documentation, then edit it. Type it directly in the field.

As applicable, cover the wound care regimen and dressing changes, interventions done today and planned next, healing progress and goals, management of contributing factors, care coordination, and the follow-up plan. Make clear what was done today versus what is planned.
Section 10: Click Mark as Complete.
A generated draft does not replace your clinical judgement — review and edit it before you sign.
Section 11 — Orders & DME: Create and send orders for DME and wound care supplies, labs, imaging, specialist referrals, and home health. Orders go to the recipient by fax or email.
Choose the order type from the tabs: DME, Labs, Imaging, Referrals, Home Health.

Select the recipient. In Select Recipient, search for the vendor, specialist, facility, or agency. If a home health agency is missing, click Add home health agency. Recipients come from your CRM, which also fills in their name, contact, fax number, and email.
Complete the order form for that order type, and check the recipient's details.
Send it. Choose Send via Fax or Send via Email, confirm, and check the transmission status to make sure it was sent.
Use Show Previous Orders to review earlier orders, then click Mark as Complete.
Sending a DME order starts the request with the vendor; the vendor or agency handles fulfillment and delivery.
Section 12 — Patient Education: The Patient Education Management area has three tabs: Assigned Materials, Education Library, and Care Bundles.
Find materials. In Education Library, search or filter by category and language, and click Preview to read a material. Select materials to assign them to the patient.

Use a care bundle. In Care Bundles, pick a bundle that fits the patient's condition (for example, Diabetic Wound Care and Prevention, Arterial Ulcer Care, General Wound Care Basics, Infection Warning Signs, Caregiver Education and Instructions, or Activity Guidelines). Preview it, then Print Bundle as a take-home handout and/or Assign Bundle to the patient.

checks.note: an example bundle name

claims.finding: Care bundles are rows loaded from education_bundles for the facility (EducationVisit.tsx:250-257), so their names depend on what each organization set up. Four of the six example names (Arterial Ulcer Care, General Wound Care Basics, Caregiver Education and Instructions, Activity Guidelines) do not appear as bundle names anywhere in the code or seed data; the seeded bundles are named differently (seed_education_bundles.sql).
claims.proposed_text: Use a care bundle. In Care Bundles, pick a bundle your organization has set up that fits the patient's condition. Preview it, then Print Bundle as a take-home handout and/or Assign Bundle to the patient.

claims.claim: Document what you taught. Complete Education Topics Covered Today. Type it or use Voice Intake. Assigning a material does not replace documenting what you actually discussed.
Document understanding. In Patient Understanding Assessment, record how well the patient or caregiver understood.
Set Next Visit Education Goals — what to reinforce at the next visit.
Mark the section complete. It then shows Patient Education Completed; click Edit Again to make changes.

Section 13 — Procedures & Supplies: This section is the final review of the procedures you documented in Section 9 before they go into the progress note and billing. You review and complete them here; you don't re-enter them.

Review the procedure entries. Wound-Specific Procedure Documentation shows the active wound; Procedure Entries lists the interventions from Section 9 with their supplies. Review each wound separately.

Check for missing fields. In Procedure Documentation & Supplies, choose a procedure under Select Intervention Performed Today. Details sync from Section 9 automatically (shown by the Auto-Sync indicator). Review any alerts about missing documentation — for sharp debridement, for example, tissue level, area debrided (cm²), hemostasis method, complications, and the compliance narrative. A recommendation such as an after-treatment photo may also appear.

Complete the procedure details. Open Review Procedure Documentation. It carries in the wound assessment (Section 7) and the intervention details (Section 9). Confirm the Procedure Summary and fill in any missing fields — for sharp debridement: the deepest Tissue Level removed, Area (cm²), Hemostasis Method, and Complications (or None).

Review the procedure note. Procedure Note (Auto-generated) carries the narrative from Section 9. Edit it, or add detail with Voice Intake. If you used Use My Exact Procedure Note in Section 9, your wording is carried forward as written.

Optional — Compliance narrative. Click Generate Compliance Note for an additional structured narrative, and review it. You can leave this blank if your procedure note already documents the procedure fully.
Review the supplies, check I have reviewed the procedure documentation where shown, and click Mark as Complete.

checks.pattern: I have reviewed the procedure documentation

claims.claim: Some fields are recommended rather than required and won't stop you finishing the visit.

Section 14 — Medication Management: Review Active Prescriptions. Prescriptions sent through DoseSpot appear here once they sync; click Refresh if a new one hasn't appeared yet. Check them before adding medications to avoid duplicates.

Select the Medication Status for this visit: Patient takes no medications, and none are needed for this visit, or All medications reviewed in facility EMR for this current visit — when the facility manages the medication list in its own EMR. This is recorded in the progress note with your name and the date, and you can still document changes or prescribe.

the facility's own system. This is recorded on the progress note
with your name and the date. You can still record a medication

claims.claim: Review Patient Allergies before prescribing. Allergies come from the patient's medical history. To add or change one, update it in the patient's chart.

checks.pattern: adds/edits go through the patient detail page or the referral

claims.claim: Reconcile Active Medications (from chart). Mark what was discontinued or changed, and add anything missing.

Add a medication manually to document it in the patient's record (name, dose, route, frequency). Prescribe electronically through the built-in DoseSpot workflow: choose the medication, enter the prescription details and refills, select the patient's pharmacy, review, and send.
Review Changes This Visit and Pharmacy Order, including any pending or queued pharmacy orders.
Section 14: Click Mark as Complete if the section isn't already complete.
Adding a medication manually records it in the chart. It does not send a prescription to a pharmacy — only the DoseSpot workflow does that.

Section 15 — Billing & Documentation: This section builds the visit's billing codes from your documentation so you can review them before signing. After you sign, the billing information goes to Billing Operations as a pre-filled CMS-1500 claim.

checks.pattern: * One CMS-1500 Box 24 service line as the auto-claim builder writes it.

claims.claim: Pull the codes. In Billing — Per-Wound Review, click Pull Codes. Medipyxis uses your clinical history, comorbidities, wound assessment, interventions, and procedure documentation to suggest ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS, and E/M codes.

When the findings are reviewed, continue to Section 17.
